svg.text: Where every wire physically goes. Only the haptic driver is on the breadboard; the IMU takes male-to-female jumpers straight to the header.
170-point mini breadboard, no power rails. A column’s five holes are joined; the centre channel splits top from bottom.
• Column 13 is +3V3: the jumper in, the diode band, motor + and the jumper on to the IMU all share that column. Column 9 is MOTOR−: collector, diode anode and the motor’s black lead.
• The IMU uses the board’s second GND pin, so only +3V3 has to be daisy-chained through the breadboard.
• Power the GY-521 from 3V3 only, and fit the diode band towards +3V3. Either mistake browns the IMU out into sleep, where it still answers on I2C and returns nothing but zeros.
